story.title: White House Removes 'Build The Wall' Game Following Tetris Copyright Concerns
story.summary: The White House has taken down a game titled 'Build The Wall' from its website after the Tetris Company raised concerns about copyright infringement. The game, which was launched recently, faced criticism from the Tetris Company, which emphasized its serious stance on copyright issues.

explore_lenses.label: What changed on the White House arcade page?
explore_lenses.title: One game was removed; the arcade remains
explore_lenses.summary: The official Arcade page now lists four games and a “Coming Soon” placeholder, rather than the five-game lineup reported at launch. “Build the Wall” is not listed, while the other games remain available.

claims.text: The current White House Arcade page lists Flappy Bill, Rio Run, Supply Line, and Trump Savings Tycoon, and does not list “Build the Wall.”
At launch, Associated Press reported that Arcade included five games, including “Build the Wall.”
The removal did not end the broader Arcade initiative, since the four other games remain on the official page.

explore_lenses.label: What do the White House and Tetris argue?
explore_lenses.title: Policy promotion versus an IP and values objection
explore_lenses.summary: The administration characterized the arcade as a way to communicate its agenda through interactive content. Tetris said it neither made nor licensed “Build the Wall,” paired its copyright warning with an objection to the game’s divisive message, and said it was reviewing the matter.

claims.text: The White House said the games were intended to innovate in telling the story of the president’s accomplishments and to resonate with Americans; digital-strategy official Kaelan Dorr called them “policy you can interact with.”
The Tetris Company said it was not involved in creating “Build the Wall” and did not authorize or license Tetris brand or intellectual property for it.
Tetris also said it believes games should bring people together rather than divide them, and that it takes copyright infringement seriously.

explore_lenses.label: What could happen next legally?
explore_lenses.title: Tetris has left its options open
explore_lenses.summary: Removing the game may reduce the immediate dispute, but it does not itself resolve whether the game used protected Tetris expression. Tetris has publicly said it is reviewing the matter, while reporting reviewed did not identify a filed lawsuit or a White House explanation for the removal.

claims.text: The Tetris Company said it was “currently reviewing the matter” when asked about possible legal action.
Reporting described the game’s former page as returning a 404 error after its removal.

Forecast: Because Tetris says it is reviewing the matter, it could decide to take no further public action, seek a private resolution, or pursue a legal claim; the company has not announced which path it will take.

story_report.summary: The White House has removed “Build the Wall,” a game added to its online Arcade shortly before it disappeared. The Tetris Company said it had not authorized use of Tetris branding or intellectual property and that it takes copyright infringement seriously, but the available reporting does not establish why the White House removed the game. Its former page reportedly returned a 404 error, while the official Arcade page continues to list four other games.

sections.heading: White House Arcade Continues Operating
sections.body: The removal did not end the White House’s broader Arcade initiative. At launch, the Arcade included five games, including “Build the Wall”; its current official page lists Flappy Bill, Rio Run, Supply Line and Trump Savings Tycoon. The White House said the games were meant to tell the story of the president’s accomplishments and resonate with Americans, while digital-strategy official Kaelan Dorr described them as “policy you can interact with.”

sections.heading: Tetris Company Challenges Game Use
sections.body: The Tetris Company said it was not involved in creating “Build the Wall” and did not authorize or license Tetris brand or intellectual property for the game. The company also said it believes games should bring people together rather than divide them. Those statements express the company’s position, but the reporting reviewed contains no judicial ruling establishing whether the game infringed copyright.

sections.heading: Tetris Company Reviews Further Action
sections.body: When asked about possible legal action, the Tetris Company said it was “currently reviewing the matter.” It has not announced whether it will take no further public action, seek a private resolution or pursue a legal claim. The White House’s removal of the game does not by itself establish that either side has chosen a further course.

unresolved.text: The available reporting does not establish the White House’s reason for removing “Build the Wall,” whether Tetris sent a formal demand, whether the game could return in revised form, or whether either side plans further action.

related_stories.summary: Trump and JD Vance are set to headline a two-day Republican convention in Dallas ahead of the November midterm elections. The event aims to energize the party's base and increase voter turnout, as midterms typically pose challenges for the party in power. Trump's focus on the convention reflects his influence within the Republican Party.

The practice of giving such gifts has been described as longstanding by a White House spokesperson.

related_stories.title: Conflicting Court Rulings Create Chaos Over Missouri's Congressional Map
related_stories.summary: A federal judge has ruled that Missouri should proceed with a new congressional map favoring Republicans, following a decision by the U.S. Supreme Court to uphold a state court ruling that directed the use of an older map. This situation has led to confusion and potential impacts on the upcoming midterm elections, as the Missouri Supreme Court has also ordered a contempt hearing regarding the secretary of state's compliance with redistricting orders.
